ddx.step1_summary:
• Chief complaint: 3-day history of persistent diarrhoea.
• Symptom details:  – Diarrhoea: watery, no visible blood, urges every ~10 minutes; neither improving nor worsening.  – Abdominal pain: central/peri-umbilical, mild-to-moderate, relieved somewhat after bowel motion; mild tenderness on self-palpation.  – Vomiting: one episode this morning after eating fruit; no haematemesis.  – Nausea present; no reported fever (only mild sweating, unsure).  – No chest pain, no dyspnoea beyond baseline asthma, able to walk/talk.  – Not drinking much, limiting food intake. 
• Past medical history: Asthma.
• Medications: Regular inhaler (brand recently changed); no other drugs reported.
• Allergies: NKDA.
• Family history: Father died of bowel (colorectal) cancer 10 years ago.
• Social history: Employed; currently staying home due to symptoms. Smoking/alcohol not discussed.
• Vital signs: Not provided.
• Examination findings (remote): Patient-reported mild central abdominal tenderness; no red-flag peritonism described.
• Labs/Imaging: None performed or reported.

V: Ischaemic colitis: sudden diarrhoea + abdominal pain could stem from transient colonic hypoperfusion, though age 48 without vascular risk factors makes this less likely.
I: Viral gastroenteritis (e.g., norovirus/rotavirus): abrupt onset, 3-day self-limited diarrhoea, vomiting, central cramps, absence of blood/fever supports this.
Bacterial food-borne enteritis (Salmonella, Campylobacter, ETEC, etc.): similar presentation after possible contaminated food; pain and vomiting present.
Appendicitis (early/gastroenteritic variant): peri-umbilical pain with nausea/vomiting can mimic, but ongoing watery stools argue against.
N: Colorectal carcinoma: family history; can cause altered bowel habit, though acute 3-day watery diarrhoea is atypical.
Small-bowel NET (carcinoid): secretory diarrhoea possible but usually chronic.
D: Lactase deficiency or other malabsorption: could cause diarrhoea but tends to be chronic or related to dairy intake.
Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency: chronic greasy stools, not acute watery.
I2: Medication-induced diarrhoea (e.g., inhaled β-agonist systemic effect or contaminant): patient suspects inhaler; physiologically unlikely but considered.
Food-borne toxin (pre-formed toxin from Staph aureus, Bacillus cereus) causing vomiting/diarrhoea within hours of ingestion.
C: Coeliac disease: immune-mediated malabsorption presenting with chronic diarrhoea.
A: Inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn’s/UC): can flare with diarrhoea and crampy pain; usually chronic, may show blood/mucus.
Food allergy (e.g., fructose intolerance) precipitating loose stools.
T: Abdominal trauma leading to visceral injury with secondary ileus/diarrhoea – no history given.
E: Hyperthyroidism: increased GI motility leads to diarrhoea; other hyper-adrenergic signs absent.
Adrenal insufficiency (Addison’s): can cause abdominal pain, diarrhoea, but additional systemic features expected.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic triad of sudden-onset watery diarrhoea, mild central abdominal cramps, and brief vomiting episode without blood or high fever; typically self-limited over a few days.
Similar presentation; patient may have ingested contaminated food; severity (repeated urges, abdominal pain) fits, though absence of fever or blood makes it slightly less likely than viral.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Irritable bowel syndrome / post-infectious functional diarrhoea
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Frequent stools with relief after defecation and association with anxiety could represent IBS, but abrupt onset only 3 days ago and accompanying vomiting favour an acute infectious process.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn’s or ulcerative colitis)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: IBD can present with diarrhoea and abdominal pain; age appropriate, but acute short course, no blood, and no systemic signs make this less probable.
Family history is a risk factor; change in bowel habit can occur, but presentation is usually chronic with weight loss or blood, not abrupt 3-day watery diarrhoea.

supporting_evidence: Sudden onset of symptoms 3 days ago
Watery diarrhoea with very frequent urges
Central crampy abdominal pain relieved by stooling
No blood in stool or vomit
opposing_evidence: Patient limiting oral intake (could confound typical course)

supporting_evidence: Abrupt onset after possible dietary exposure (uncertain food quality)
Abdominal pain, diarrhoea and vomiting combination
opposing_evidence: No fever, chills or dysenteric blood
No specific history of undercooked meat/unrefrigerated food
Course not clearly severe or worsening

supporting_evidence: No alarming GI red-flags (blood, weight loss)
opposing_evidence: Very acute onset (typical IBS is chronic & recurrent)
No extra-intestinal manifestations, weight loss or fever
No rectal bleeding, weight loss, anaemia, or chronic change in bowel habit
